changes_vs_current: Scope decision: answers are what players type, mostly resort/brand level. 'Disney World' covers Walt Disney World and Magic Kingdom (alias); Epcot, Hollywood Studios, Animal Kingdom, California Adventure and Islands of Adventure stay separate items. 'Universal Studios' covers Universal Hollywood/Orlando/Florida; Universal Studios Japan is its own item. Chains (Six Flags, SeaWorld, Busch Gardens, Legoland) are one item with park names as aliases. No bare 'disney' alias; aliases checked for collisions. Computed order (avg position over 4 people sources, missing = list length+5): 1 Disneyland 1.38, 2 Disney World 1.62, 3 Universal Studios 5.75, 4 Epcot 7.25, 5 Hollywood Studios 8.25, 6 SeaWorld 8.75, 7 Animal Kingdom 9.5, 8 Six Flags 12.0, 9 Busch Gardens 12.5, 10 Islands of Adventure 12.75, 11 California Adventure 13.0, 12 Knott's 13.5, 13 Cedar Point 14.75, 14 Disneyland Paris 15.5, 15 Universal Studios Japan 15.75, 16 Tokyo Disney 16.25, 17 Hersheypark 17.5, 18 Kings Island 17.75, 19 Legoland 17.75, 20 Hong Kong Disneyland 18.0, 21 Dollywood 18.25, 22 Shanghai Disneyland 18.75, 23 Chimelong Ocean Kingdom 19.0, 24 Universal Studios Beijing 20.25, 25 Everland 20.5, 27 Silver Dollar City 21.0. Revision 2, after the coordinator's gut check (Disney World, Disneyland, Universal Studios, Six Flags, Cedar Point, SeaWorld, Busch Gardens, Knott's, Dollywood, Hersheypark, Legoland, Epcot). Question checked: does any naming/favorite measure (not fame or attendance) put Cedar Point, Busch Gardens, Knott's or Dollywood below Hollywood Studios, Animal Kingdom, Islands of Adventure and California Adventure? No. None of the sources read is a general-public naming/favorite poll. The sub-parks are lifted only by YouGov fame, TEA per-park attendance and the Sudoku search/hashtag/TripAdvisor index (Animal Kingdom 5, Hollywood Studios 9 vs Cedar Point 10, Islands of Adventure 12, Knott's 14, Busch 16, which is search interest, not naming). The favorite-type sources rate the regional parks high and leave out the sub-parks: NAPHA's favorite park is Dollywood (Busch Gardens Williamsburg tied first in 2021), and Quartz 2025 ranks resorts first, then Cedar Point 3, Hersheypark 4, Knott's 5, Busch 6, Dollywood 7, SeaWorld 8, Legoland 10. So the gut-check rule applies. Moves: (1) Disney World and Disneyland flip to 1 and 2. Disney World has the largest attendance (Magic Kingdom #1 worldwide, plus Epcot/HS/AK under the same resort name), is better liked on YouGov (popularity 63% vs 60%, Magic Kingdom 65%) and is #1 on both gut checks. Disneyland leads only on fame (98 vs 97) and the search index. (2) Six Flags 8 -> 4: both YouGov sources put it 4th (brand fame 94%). Attendance and search sources count only Magic Mountain, which splits a 40-park chain. (3) SeaWorld 6, Busch Gardens 7, Cedar Point 8, Knott's 9, Dollywood 10 (from 6, 9, 13, 12, 21) are moved ahead of the four sub-parks per the gut check; no naming source contradicts it. Cedar Point is above Knott's: both gut checks put it there, and it ranks above Knott's in Sudoku (10 vs 14), Quartz (3 vs 5) and Westgate. Knott's leads only on fame/attendance. (4) Hersheypark 17 -> 11 and Legoland 19 -> 12: both are in the coordinator's gut-check 12. The only sources that place them lower are fame/attendance measures, and Quartz has them at 4 and 10. (5) Hollywood Studios 5 -> 13, Animal Kingdom 7 -> 14, Islands of Adventure 10 -> 15, California Adventure 11 -> 16: kept as separate items but placed after the parks people name on their own, because most people fold them into 'Disney World'/'Universal'/'Disneyland'. Epcot stays at 5 (it is in both gut checks and named on its own). (6) Overseas Disney/Universal parks and Kings Island keep their relative order at 17-21 (Disneyland Paris, USJ, Tokyo Disney, Kings Island, HK Disneyland). Kings Island stays below the top 12 because YouGov fame is 54% and it is TEA NA #15 and Sudoku #21. (7) Chimelong Ocean Kingdom and Universal Studios Beijing are left off: they have attendance data only and are absent from YouGov's 218-entry US attraction list, which does include Everland, Lotte World and Ocean Park. Silver Dollar City (Sudoku #15, Quartz #9, Westgate #5) is #23 and Everland (2 sources) #24. Epic Universe is left off for lack of data. USA Today 10Best could not be fetched and is not cited.
confidence: High for 1-4. Medium for 5-12: the order of SeaWorld/Busch/Cedar Point/Knott's/Dollywood/Hersheypark/Legoland follows the gut check plus the critic sources, because no general-public favorite poll exists. Medium-low for 13-24: sub-parks placed by judgment that people fold them into the resort name; overseas parks rank on attendance alone. Caveats: YouGov Buzz source is from 2011; Wikipedia pageviews/Google Trends were rate-limited and not used.
